art.title: The Cradle
art.credit: Public domain · image via Wikimedia Commons
art.story: Berthe Morisot's sister Edma watches her baby daughter sleep, chin resting on her hand. A thin veil of gauze hangs over the cradle like a tent, and through it we glimpse the baby's face. Edma had painted too, but gave it up when she married; Berthe kept going, and became one of the founders of Impressionism. She showed this picture at the group's very first exhibition, in 1874, the only woman among them.
